title: Transition into Data Analytics
subtitle: A self-study route in the order I'd learn it today.

know_first.heading: Before you start
know_first.intro: Hi, I'm Katie. I'm sharing my experience on how I transitioned into data analytics and here are my resources.
points: Self-study is challenging. There's no syllabus, instructor or classmates, so you find your own answers and fix your own errors.
If time is tight, self-study may not be the best route. With consistency and determination it's still doable.
Entry-level roles are competitive. A portfolio of real projects (the last step) matters more than any certificate.
know_first.disclaimer: No course here sponsors me. Disclosure: I previously worked on SQL content for DataLemur, which appears in the tutorial and interview prep sections. ★ Katie's pick marks resources I've tried myself and recommend.

steps.title: Start with a general course
steps.lead: If you're curious about a data career but don't know where to begin, take a general data analytics course first, like Google's. It gives you an overview of the field, an introduction to the skills and tools you'll learn, a study-at-your-own-pace format and a certificate for your resume.
paras: Google's covers spreadsheets, SQL (BigQuery), Tableau and R, and has since added AI-assisted modules. On average people finish it in 2 to 6 months, and the faster you finish, the less you pay.
You don't need both options below. Pick one to start, then move on to the steps after it.

callout.title: Know what a certificate can and can't do
callout.text: This course is marketed as a job-ready programme. In my experience that isn't true. One course is not enough to get an entry-level job or pass a technical interview. At most it contributed 5 to 10% of my learning, so use it as a starting point and keep going with the steps below.

items.d: A general overview of data analytics and the tools you'll use. Covers spreadsheets, SQL (BigQuery), Tableau and R, now with AI-assisted modules. Self-paced.

items.n: Alex the Analyst: Data Analyst Bootcamp
items.d: I highly recommend this free YouTube bootcamp. It covers SQL, Excel, Tableau, Power BI, Python and portfolio projects. Excellent if you're new or want to sharpen any of these tools.

steps.title: Excel and Google Sheets
steps.lead: Excel is still one of the most common skills in data analyst job ads, and you'll likely use it every week at work. Don't skip it. Alex the Analyst's bootcamp (first step) also has an Excel section.

items.d: Google Cloud's short beginner course on Sheets. Free to take, with a paid option for the certificate, quizzes and projects.
Short exercises with answers for each chapter of the W3Schools Excel tutorial.
His Excel playlist, with videos for beginners through more experienced users.
Excel tutorials from Leila Gharani, a Microsoft MVP.
A Google Sheets tutorial from Kevin Stratvert.
Google Sheets tutorials from Leila Gharani.

items: Lookup: XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH.
Conditional formulas: SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS, IF, IFS.
Dynamic arrays: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE.
Text and date manipulation.
PivotTables and PivotCharts.
Power Query for cleaning and transforming data.
Data validation and conditional formatting.
Google Sheets QUERY, ARRAYFORMULA, FILTER and IMPORTRANGE.
Basic automation using Office Scripts or Google Apps Script.
skills.note: Power Query is particularly valuable for analysts who repeatedly receive CSV files or Excel exports that need cleaning and combining.

steps.title: Statistics
steps.lead: You only need the basics: averages and spread, distributions, sampling and the difference between correlation and causation. Study them up front or pick them up as they come up in your learning.

items.d: Josh Starmer's Statistics Fundamentals playlist covers probability, distributions, sampling and hypothesis testing.
Free lessons and practice on graphs, summary statistics, linear regression and hypothesis testing.
A free, self-paced course on statistics, data types and storytelling with data. You need a free Tableau account to access it.

steps.title: SQL
steps.lead: SQL is the easiest and most essential skill for any data analyst role. It's how you extract, manipulate and analyze data, and once you know it, other tools get easier (Tableau's calculated fields use SQL-style logic).

items.d: Alex the Analyst's SQL series, in three levels.

links.d: 4-part series on creating tables, inserting data and querying data.
5-part series on joins, subqueries and functions.
4-part series on window functions, recursive queries and common table expressions.

items.d: A 3-hour course that covers the basics of SQL.
30+ free lessons split into basic, intermediate and advanced. You can run queries in your browser. I previously worked on its SQL content.
Starts with core SQL commands, joins and aggregations, then moves to subqueries, temp tables and window functions.
A free GitHub course built from Danny Ma's live training at ODSC Asia Pacific 2021. You work with a cryptocurrency trading dataset.
A free structured SQL path with lessons and practice questions, from the basics to window functions.
Business-style questions on real data, good for window functions.
I took this course myself and it improved my SQL massively. Taught by Danny Ma of Data With Danny.
Absolute beginners; interactive lessons.
A free interactive book with no ads or sign-up. You learn by running queries against a real dataset, about 30 minutes per chapter.
Interactive game that teaches you SQL basics by solving a murder case. Runs in your browser.
8 different SQL case studies designed to improve your SQL skills.
Real-world SQL interview questions with detailed solutions and explanations.
Large bank of interview questions across SQL and Python. Free tier plus paid plans.

items.n: Practical SQL: A Beginner's Guide to Storytelling with Data
items.d: By Anthony DeBarros.

items.n: SQL for Data Analysis: Advanced Techniques for Transforming Data into Insights
items.d: By Cathy Tanimura.

groups.name: Which SQL software to use
groups.note: When you want your own local setup, these are the common free choices (they're called SQL flavours). The basics are the same across all of them, so pick the one your course uses and learn the differences later.

items.d: Windows, Mac and Linux.
Windows and Mac.
Alex Freberg's course uses it. The free Express edition is enough for learning.

items: Querying: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT.
Aggregation: COUNT, SUM, AVG, GROUP BY, HAVING.
Joins: INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN, and when to use each.
Conditional logic: CASE WHEN.
Subqueries and CTEs.
Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD, running totals.
Dates and strings: date functions, string functions.
Cleaning data: NULLs, duplicates, DISTINCT, COALESCE.
skills.note: Joins and window functions come up most often in interviews.

steps.title: Tableau or Power BI
steps.lead: Tableau and Power BI are business intelligence and data visualization tools for building interactive dashboards and reports. Pick one first, because the skills transfer.
paras: Which one? Pick one to learn. I recommend Power BI because it's free to download and most job ads in Malaysia use it.

items.d: Tableau's desktop app, available as a 14-day trial.
Free, but everything you save there is public.
Free to download on Windows only. On a Mac, use Power BI in the browser.
A YouTube channel with many helpful Tableau tutorials.
Alex the Analyst's beginner Tableau series: installing Tableau and building a first chart, calculated fields, more chart types, joins, then a full project.
Free tutorials and videos from Tableau.

items.n: Codecademy: Learn Tableau for Data Visualization
items.d: A short beginner course on building Tableau dashboards.
Community-led meetups, online and in person, where you can learn and ask questions. Sign up for a free account to join.
Tableau Public features a community visualization most weekdays. Many workbooks can be downloaded to see how they were built.
A weekly challenge to re-create a data visualization. Started in the Tableau community and also runs Power BI challenges.
A guide to explaining data clearly with charts and a story. A 10th anniversary edition came out in January 2026.

steps.title: Python
steps.lead: Python is not always required for data analysts. In some companies it's only good-to-have, in others it's a must-have. Learn it if you're aiming at tech companies or at data scientist or data engineer roles.
paras: Either way, get comfortable with SQL, a spreadsheet tool and one BI tool first.
For setup, Alex's bootcamp includes a video on installing Jupyter Notebook and Anaconda. Kaggle's free notebooks also run in your browser with nothing to install.

items.d: A beginner-friendly full Python course of about 6 hours.
A 4-hour course on the Python data analysis workflow. Covers NumPy, pandas, data cleaning and reading data from CSV, SQL and Excel.

items.n: Harvard CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python
items.d: Free via Harvard's OpenCourseWare. Paid certificate options are on edX.
Short hands-on micro-courses in the browser on real datasets.
Covers the full data analysis process with NumPy, pandas and Matplotlib on real datasets.
A free structured Python path covering pandas, data wrangling and interview-style problems.
A short micro-course on cleaning messy data: missing values, scaling, parsing dates and fixing inconsistent entries. About 4 hours.
A short micro-course on charts in Python with Seaborn. About 4 hours.

items.n: Maven Analytics: Python Foundations for Data Analysis
items.d: Hands-on, project-based course on the core building blocks of Python for data analysis, using Jupyter notebooks.

items.n: Maven Analytics: Data Analysis with Python: NumPy & Pandas
items.d: Project-based course on NumPy and pandas. You explore, transform, aggregate and join data, and import files like CSV and Excel.
Python practice problems you can solve in your browser.

items.n: Wes McKinney's Python for Data Analysis
items.d: The pandas creator's own book, updated for Python 3.10 and pandas 1.4. Also free to read online on the author's website. Best as a reference once you know the basics.

items: Basics: variables, data types, loops, functions, lists and dictionaries.
pandas: loading CSV and Excel files, filtering, sorting.
Cleaning data: missing values, duplicates, data types, dates and text.
Combining and summarising: groupby, merge, pivot tables.
NumPy basics.
Charts with matplotlib or seaborn.
Working in Jupyter notebooks.
Loading SQL query results into pandas.
skills.note: pandas is the part analysts use most, so spend most of your time there.

steps.title: Build a portfolio on GitHub
steps.lead: A portfolio shows potential employers or clients what you can actually do, and GitHub is a good place to keep it. Start with the guide, then use my own portfolio as a model for structure and content.
paras: Once you have a project, practise explaining it. Below are datasets to build on.

items.n: How to create a GitHub portfolio
items.d: My step-by-step guide to setting up a portfolio on GitHub.
For inspiration on structure and content.
Malaysia's open data portal, with datasets from federal and state agencies. Download them or connect through an API.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia's open data on population, prices, labour and GDP. CSV and Parquet downloads, free to reuse under a Creative Commons licence.
Daily ridership data for public transport services across Malaysia. Good raw material for a dashboard.

items.n: Bank Negara Malaysia rates and statistics
items.d: Interest rates and other central bank statistics. Download as CSV or use the API. Credit "Source: Bank Negara Malaysia" if you publish your work.
The Ministry of Health's official COVID-19 data on GitHub, including cases, hospital admissions and vaccinations as CSV files. It's historical, so best for practising time series and data cleaning.
Economic, health and other indicators for Malaysia and every other country. Download as Excel or CSV from any data page.
A huge library of public datasets. You can browse without an account, but you need a free account to download.
A search engine for datasets, wherever they're hosted. Use it when you have a topic but no data.
Free sample datasets picked by Maven instructors, from flight delays to movie ratings. Good raw material for a portfolio project.

ai.title: Using AI along the way
ai.lead: AI tools can now write SQL, Excel formulas and Python for you. That makes the fundamentals more important, not less, because you need to be able to tell when the output is wrong.
points: Learn SQL first. Then use AI as a tutor and a second pair of eyes, and always read and run the SQL or code it gives you.
Don't paste confidential company data or personal information into a public AI tool.
Google's Data Analytics certificate now includes modules on using AI for cleaning data, formulas and visualizations.
